pairs.current_prompt: Describe your verification approach and what you concluded.

examples.answer: I ran the supported browsers through the main purchase flow and all checks passed. That establishes that every browser workflow is defect-free.
examples.review_reason: The conclusion extends beyond the checked flows.

examples.answer: I ran the supported browsers through the main purchase flow and all checks passed. That establishes that those checked flows worked under the tested conditions.
examples.review_reason: The conclusion is explicitly limited to the checked flows and tested conditions.

pairs.current_prompt: Explain your storage decision and its tradeoff.

examples.answer: I chose synchronous replication. It reduced the risk of losing acknowledged writes but added write latency. I accepted the latency because durability matters.
examples.review_reason: The consequential prioritization is asserted without examining the balance.

examples.answer: I chose synchronous replication. It reduced the risk of losing acknowledged writes but added write latency. I accepted it because measured latency remained within our agreed limit and losing acknowledged writes would breach our recovery requirement.
examples.review_reason: The benefit and cost are balanced against relevant requirements.

pairs.current_prompt: Describe your change and the result you observed.

examples.answer: I introduced a deployment checklist. Rollbacks decreased in the following month. That proves the checklist was the sole cause of the decrease.
examples.review_reason: The observation is used to make an exclusive causal claim.

examples.answer: I introduced a deployment checklist. Rollbacks decreased in the following month. That is the result we observed; I have not isolated the checklist's contribution.
examples.review_reason: The descriptive observation is reported without an unsupported causal guarantee.
